summary: Migrated all inline badge HTML in the 4 target files to UI.badge() calls.

views/project-list.js: replaced runnerBadge() inline span with UI.badge('runner-{safeRunner}', label). The badge-runner base class is dropped (visual parity maintained since each specific runner variant has its own full CSS rule).

views/run-log.js: migrated 8 badge instances — dry-run badge in run_start; result badge in stage_complete (also changed result variable to avoid pre-escaping); pipeline status badge in pipeline_result; old/new status badges in wp_status_change; dry-run badge in dry_run, dry_run_no_ledger, dry_run_complete. One exception: the cross-WP badge in the tool_call case was left inline because it requires a title tooltip attribute that UI.badge() does not support.
views/orchestrator.js: replaced _buildQueueHtml() statusBadgeHtml inline span with UI.badge(status, _orchStatusLabel(status)).

js/orchestrator-widgets.js: replaced renderStatusCard() status badge with UI.badge(meta.cls, meta.label); replaced renderProgressBadge() inline span with UI.badge(mapping.color, mapping.icon + ' ' + rawLabel) — removed pre-escaping of rawLabel since UI.badge() handles escaping internally.
Browser verification: no JS errors in console across project-list, orchestrator, and run-log views; 30 badge elements rendered correctly in run-log; PASS badge displays in green at stage_complete.

comments.note: run-log.js line ~271: The tool_call cross-WP badge (⚠ cross-WP: ...) was intentionally left inline because UI.badge() does not accept a title/tooltip attribute. If UI.badge() ever gains an optional attrs parameter, this instance should be migrated.

views/project-list.js runnerBadge(): migration dropped the base .badge-runner class (was: 'badge badge-runner badge-runner-{type}', now: 'badge badge-runner-{type}'). Visually identical because every specific runner variant has its own full color rule. However, if CSS ever adds a rule that relies on .badge-runner being present alongside a specific variant, the change would need to be revisited.

js/orchestrator-widgets.js renderProgressBadge(): the old code pre-escaped the label with escapeHtml() before interpolating it into an HTML string, which was internally consistent but slightly confusing. The new code passes the raw string to UI.badge() which applies escapeHtml() internally — a cleaner pattern that aligns with the UI.badge() contract.

summary: Build check: DEV GUI server starts cleanly on port 3425 (tsx gui/server.ts); components.js serves UI.badge() definition; all view scripts load without syntax errors.

AC1 (project-list.js): runnerBadge() calls UI.badge('runner-{safeRunner}', label) producing 'badge badge-runner-{type}' (2 classes — base badge-runner correctly dropped). statusBadge() delegates to UI.badge(status, status) in utils.js. No dry-run badge in project-list (not applicable at list view). DOM verified: <span class='badge badge-runner-orchestrator'> and <span class='badge badge-complete'> generated correctly.

AC2 (run-log.js): 8 badge instances migrated to UI.badge(). Single intentional exception at line 271 (cross-WP tool_call badge with title tooltip attribute) is documented and acceptable. The run-stage-badge header element uses a separate CSS class system (run-stage-badge, not badge badge-*) and is outside the badge migration scope.
AC3 (orchestrator.js): _buildQueueHtml() status badge migrated to UI.badge(status, _orchStatusLabel(status)). status values are 'pending'|'started'|'dead' with correct CSS class coverage.
AC4 (orchestrator-widgets.js): renderStatusCard() uses UI.badge(meta.cls, meta.label); renderProgressBadge() uses UI.badge(mapping.color, icon+rawLabel). All color values are hardcoded safe strings.

AC5 (dark mode): All 14 badge types verified via DOM inspection in dark mode — dry-run (#3b0764/#d8b4fe), pass (#14532d/#86efac), fail (#450a0a/#fca5a5), neutral (#1f2937/#9ca3af), pending (#422006/#fcd34d), started (#052e16/#4ade80), dead (#450a0a/#fca5a5), info/success/error/warning, all 4 runner variants. All match defined dark token values exactly.
AC6 (no JS errors): Zero pageerror events captured during navigation through project-list and orchestrator views.

Script loading order verified: components.js (defines UI) loads at position 7, before all view scripts (position 8+). Regression confirmed: no inline <span class='badge badge-*'> remaining in the 4 target files except the documented exception at run-log.js:271.

comments.note: components.js UI.badge(): _normaliseType() is not HTML-escaped — the type argument is interpolated directly into the class attribute (e.g. class='badge badge-{type}'). Current callers all pass server-controlled enum strings so there is no XSS risk, and the code documents this assumption. If UI.badge() is ever called with user-supplied input, the type argument must be sanitized at the call site. Not a regression introduced by WP-002 (inherited from WP-001).

orchestrator.js _buildQueueHtml(): UI.badge(status, ...) passes entry.effectiveStatus directly without explicit guard to the 3 known values ('pending'|'started'|'dead'). An unexpected effectiveStatus value would render a badge with class 'badge badge-{unexpected}' with no matching CSS rule (falls back to base .badge styling — visually unstyled but not broken). Not a regression from WP-002.

QA note: The running GUI server at port 3420 is from the STABLE workspace, not DEV. Visual verification was performed against a fresh DEV server started at port 3425. Visual parity was confirmed for all migrated badge classes across both light and dark modes.

summary: Reviewed all 4 migrated files (project-list.js, run-log.js, orchestrator.js, orchestrator-widgets.js) against maintainability, best practices, performance, and future-context dimensions.

Migration is clean and consistent. All 8 badge instances in run-log.js, the queue status badge in orchestrator.js, and the two badge sites in orchestrator-widgets.js are correctly delegating to UI.badge(). The single documented exception at run-log.js:271 (cross-WP tool_call badge with title tooltip) is a legitimate architectural carve-out.

Fix-Forward applied: all four file header 'Depends on' comments updated to include 'UI (components.js)' — the badge migration introduced this runtime dependency in every file but none of the headers were updated.

No blocking issues. QA-flagged items (_normaliseType class injection, effectiveStatus unguarded) are pre-existing patterns inherited from WP-001 and correctly scoped as low-priority inherited notes, not regressions.
runnerBadge() in project-list.js correctly handles falsy, 'unknown', known, and novel runner values; the || fallback for unknown strings is reachable and correct.
renderProgressBadge() uses raw action strings as badge labels — intentional and documented; UI.badge() escapes them safely.

comments.note: Updated 'Depends on' header comment in all 4 migrated files to add 'UI (components.js)'. The badge migration introduced UI as a runtime dependency in each file but the file-header dependency declarations were not updated. Non-behavioral comment fix; QA validation remains intact.

run-log.js:271 cross-WP badge is the only intentional inline badge surviving the migration. If UI.badge() ever gains an optional attrs/title parameter (a natural future enhancement), this should be the first migration target.

orchestrator.js _buildQueueHtml(): effectiveStatus is passed directly to UI.badge() type argument with only a || 'pending' null guard. Since effectiveStatus is server-controlled enum data the risk is negligible, but a future defensive guard (whitelist check) would be consistent with the principle of not trusting intermediate data shapes. Not a regression from WP-002.
